# Writing System

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:WritingSystem`](gmeow-WritingSystem.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/WritingSystem>
- **Category:** class
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/language`](../../slices/language.md)
- **Box roles:** [TBox role](../boxes/tbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

A first-class system for visually or tactilely representing language — a script: Latin, Han (kanji), Hiragana, Katakana, Arabic, Braille, or a bespoke conlang/AI script. Carries [`gmeow:scriptCode`](../properties/gmeow-scriptCode.md) (ISO 15924 when one exists, else a bespoke identifier), a type ([`gmeow:writingSystemType`](../properties/gmeow-writingSystemType.md)) and a direction ([`gmeow:textDirection`](../properties/gmeow-textDirection.md)). Bound to the languages that use it — co-equally and simultaneously — through [`gmeow:WritingSystemUsage`](gmeow-WritingSystemUsage.md); bespoke and non-linear scripts (Ithkuil) are first-class.

## Structure

**Subclass of:** [`gmeow:InformationObject`](gmeow-InformationObject.md)

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:WritingSystem`](gmeow-WritingSystem.md) as a specialized kind of [`gmeow:InformationObject`](gmeow-InformationObject.md). Add statement metadata or a standpoint when the assertion needs provenance, confidence, or vantage.

### Notation Systems

- **Source:** [`slices/core/notation/examples/notation-systems.ttl`](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/slices/core/notation/examples/notation-systems.ttl)
- **Examples catalog:** [open in catalog](../../examples/index.md#example-slices-core-notation-examples-notation-systems)#example-slices-core-notation-examples-notation-systems

```turtle
# --- A script IS a notation system: the Latin writing system, viewed as the
#     encoding notation it provides.
ex:latin a gmeow:WritingSystem ;
    rdfs:label                  "Latin script"@en ;
    gmeow:writingSystemAsNotation ex:latinNotation .
```

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use to mint a script as a first-class object — Latin, Han, Arabic, Braille, or a bespoke conlang/AI script — separately from the languages that use it, so one language written in several scripts and one script shared across languages are both modelled co-equally.

### Avoid when

- Avoid folding the script into the [`Language`](gmeow-Language.md) itself (a language is not its script) and avoid treating ISO 15924 as identity; mint a bespoke [`scriptCode`](../properties/gmeow-scriptCode.md) when no standard code exists rather than refusing the script.

### How to use

- Mint the [`WritingSystem`](gmeow-WritingSystem.md), give it a [`gmeow:scriptCode`](../properties/gmeow-scriptCode.md), [`gmeow:writingSystemType`](../properties/gmeow-writingSystemType.md), and [`gmeow:textDirection`](../properties/gmeow-textDirection.md), and bind it to each language that uses it through a [`gmeow:WritingSystemUsage`](gmeow-WritingSystemUsage.md) relator rather than a direct attribute, so co-equal multi-script usage is first-class.

### Examples

- ex:scriptLatin a [`gmeow:WritingSystem`](gmeow-WritingSystem.md); [`gmeow:scriptCode`](../properties/gmeow-scriptCode.md) "Latn".
